about:
Telink Semiconductor is headquartered in Tustin, California, and was founded in 2014. The company operates as a fabless semiconductor supplier, designing and marketing multi-protocol wireless system-on-chip (SoC) solutions for the Internet of Things. No founder names or ownership structure are disclosed in the available sources.

The company develops SoCs that integrate Bluetooth Low Energy, Bluetooth Classic, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Wi-Fi 6, Amazon Sidewalk, and 2.4 GHz proprietary protocols. Product families include the TL323X series for Matter and Amazon Sidewalk, the automotive-grade TL3225 series, the high-performance TL721X series, and the TL3228 targeting 8 KHz wireless gaming peripherals. Telink supports development with software development kits (SDKs), an integrated development environment, hardware design guidelines, reference designs, a product selection tool, and a technical forum staffed by its engineers.

Telink’s solutions are used in smart home devices such as lighting and door locks, wireless audio and gaming accessories requiring low latency, human input devices including keyboards and mice, universal remote controls for major smart TV and set-top box brands, industrial IoT nodes, and electronic shelf labels for smart retail. The company cites deployments with some of the world’s largest smart TV, set-top box, and OTT box manufacturers.

Telink emphasizes ultra-low power efficiency, multi-protocol coexistence on a single chip, and certification to Thread, OpenThread, and Matter standards as key differentiators. It positions its one-stop development ecosystem — silicon, software, tools, and direct engineering support — as a way to accelerate customers’ time-to-market.
